questions.statement: A container is a small virtual machine with its own kernel.
questions.explanation: A container is a process on the host's kernel that the kernel isolates. A VM has its own kernel on emulated hardware.

questions.statement: Many containers of the same image share its layers on disk.
A container lives as long as its main process.
Kubernetes uses Docker itself to run containers.
questions.explanation: Kubernetes uses containerd, but it runs exactly the images that docker build makes.

questions.statement: COPY in a Dockerfile can only take files from the build context.
Running as root inside a container is safe because the container is isolated.
questions.explanation: All containers share one kernel. Root in a container, with the wrong settings, is close to root on the host.

questions.statement: docker stop sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10 seconds.
